answer: A skill I taught myself during my university years was cooking, which I had always avoided out of sheer laziness. At home, my mother has always done the cooking, so I never really had to lift a finger in the kitchen. That changed when I moved to Dhaka for my BBA and started sharing a small flat with three other students. Living away from home, I got tired of eating out and decided it was time to become [[self-sufficient]]. I started with simple recipes from online videos, and my early attempts were genuinely disastrous. There was a real [[learning curve]], and I burned more meals than I care to admit, which was quite [[discouraging]] at first. I also rang my mother constantly, asking how much turmeric to add or how long to cook the lentils. But I [[persevered]], and gradually things started to improve. What I found most rewarding was the moment I cooked a proper chicken curry that actually tasted good, and my flatmates asked for more. Beyond the practical benefit, cooking turned out to be surprisingly relaxing, almost [[therapeutic]] after a stressful day. I also realised how much work my mother had been doing for years without a word of complaint. It gave me a real sense of independence and pride. Honestly, learning this skill changed my daily life for the better, and it reminded me that most things become manageable if you are willing to fail a few times first. Now that I am back home, I even cook for the family occasionally.

followUps.answer: Now and then. My mother still rules the kitchen, but on Fridays I sometimes make a simple curry or fried rice for everyone. My younger sister is my harshest critic, which keeps me honest.

followUps.q: What skill would you like to learn next?
followUps.answer: I'd love to learn to play the guitar properly. I listen to a lot of music, and being able to play a few songs for friends and family would be really satisfying.
